REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - FEBRUARY 9, 2023 - 07:00 P.M.
SIERRA ROOM – CERRITOS CENTER FOR THE PERFORMING ARTS
18000 PARK PLAZA DRIVE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
COUNCILMEMBER SOLANKI WILL PARTICIPATE VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM YADAV STREET, UPLETA, GUJARAT, INDIA, AND THIS AGENDA WILL BE POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the Sierra Room will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021) and City Council Resolution No. 2022-10 adopted pursuant thereto, this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Sierra Room subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Troop 693.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Bruce Barrows
  Mayor/Chair Chuong Vo

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  None.

5B.  Review and consideration of appointments, removals, and filling of scheduled or unscheduled
  vacancies on the Cerritos Advisory Boards (2022-24 term) (COUNCIL).

  There was no action taken on this item.

5C.  Informational update on the City’s response to the COVID-19 pandemic and other City
  events, services, and programs.

  An informational update was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no action taken on this item.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  David Pylman commented on perceptions of the public regarding the upcoming City
  Manager vacancy and expressed his concern regarding the potential of allowing
  additional drive-through restaurants in the community.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Sheila Gibbons expressed concerns regarding code violations in the community,
  particularly those occurring in the Walmart parking lot.

  Thomas Simonovski requested the City consider support of and investment in a
  proposed ABC Unified School District aquatics center.

  Case van der Linden requested the City institute deep root watering techniques on
  existing and new trees.

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed to the City Manager to provide the City Council with

  to public speaker Mr. Case van der Linden.

  Center for the Performing Arts, addressing the long lines at the bar/concession, and
  suggested scheduling contemporary performers at the venue to increase revenue.

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the following:

  1. The goals of the City of Cerritos expanded social media program, listed as follows:

  a.  Increase the channels used to communicate with the City’s various publics,
  including residents, current and prospective local business owners, people
  who work in the City and community organizations.
  b.  Reach a broader audience by sharing information with people who access
  social media for news and updates.
  c.  Announce news about City initiatives and developments.
  d.  Enhance transparency by posting information across multiple platforms.
  e.  Instantaneously disseminate accurate information.
  f.  Communicate public safety information.
  g.  Promote City programs, events and services.
  h.  Encourage economic development; and

  2. The launch of the official City of Cerritos presence on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter,
  and LinkedIn in February 2023, without allowing commenting, for a trial period of six
  (6) to twelve (12) months. Discontinue posting content on the City’s Facebook group
  once the City’s Facebook page is online; and

  3. The launch of a Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts presence on Instagram,
  without allowing commenting, for a trial period of six (6) to twelve (12) months; and

  4. The City of Cerritos Digital Communications Policy; and

  5. Expenditures of $1,794 for a subscription to ArchiveSocial social media archiving
  software and a $96 for Twitter Blue subscription; and

  6. Schedule an agenda report for City Council review of the outcomes of the trial period
  six (6) to twelve (12) months after the launch of the expanded social media program
  (COUNCIL).
